title: Relationship and societal marketing
log: 2026-10-29T12:22:32Z write: the API refused it in the chapter request, so it is written on its own next

match.reason: No point in the bank covers relationship or societal marketing; corporate social responsibility is a related but different idea about a business's wider duties, not a marketing approach.

draft.title: Relationship and societal marketing
card: building a long-term bond with customers so they keep buying and stay loyal. It aims to keep customers, not just make one sale.
Businesses may use loyalty programs, personal service and regular contact to build the bond. Loyal customers tend to buy again and may recommend the business to others.
an approach that weighs what customers want, what the business earns and what is good for society. Society includes the community and the environment.
A business using societal marketing might cut packaging waste or avoid selling products that harm people, even when this costs it some sales.
draft.remember: Relationship marketing keeps customers loyal. Societal marketing also weighs the good of society.

a.q: Which action is the best example of relationship marketing?
opts: A bookshop gives members a points card and personal picks
A bookshop cuts prices for one week to clear old stock
A bookshop runs a billboard ad to announce its opening
A bookshop moves to a larger site beside a train station
a.why: A points card and personal picks aim to build a lasting bond so customers keep returning. A one-week price cut is aimed at a single burst of sales, not at loyalty over time.
a.clue: Which action is aimed at keeping customers over time?

b.q: Tane runs a snack company in Newcastle. He stops using plastic wrappers that harm local waterways, even though the change cuts his profit a little. Which approach does this show?
opts: Societal marketing, as it weighs the good of society
Relationship marketing, as it builds customer loyalty
Production approach, as it focuses on making the goods
Selling approach, as it pushes the goods to customers
b.why: Tane gives up some profit to reduce harm to the community and environment, which is societal marketing. Relationship marketing is the most tempting wrong answer, but the change is aimed at society's good, not at building a bond with customers.
b.clue: Who benefits from the change besides the customers?

a.best: A bookshop gives members a points card and personal picks

b.best: Societal marketing, as it weighs the good of society
